query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing approximately 50 at.% Pt into an equiatomic FeCoNiMnCu high-entropy alloy will promote the formation of an L10 ordered intermetallic phase that reduces the cubic symmetry and enhances spin–orbit coupling, thereby increasing the coercive field relative to the undoped alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeCoNiMnCu high-entropy alloy with a predominantly disordered, high-symmetry FCC (or near cubic) structure.
generation.intervention: Add approximately 50 at.% Pt during alloy synthesis to induce L10 ordering.
generation.conditions: Samples prepared under similar sputtering (or equivalent synthesis) and rapid thermal annealing conditions that allow phase formation; the effect is anticipated when the Pt addition is sufficient to stabilize a single high-entropy L10 phase.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a chemically ordered L10 intermetallic phase with tetragonal symmetry.
generation.mechanism: The Pt atoms substitute into the lattice, lowering the symmetry from cubic to tetragonal (L10 order) and introducing strong spin–orbit coupling. This enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy increases domain wall pinning, thereby raising the coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Pt-doped alloy will exhibit a significantly higher coercive field compared to the baseline FeCoNiMnCu alloy, with microstructural evidence confirming the L10 phase.
generation.baseline: FeCoNiMnCu alloy without Pt addition, exhibiting a high-symmetry FCC (or disordered) structure with lower intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
generation.boundary: The increase in coercivity is expected only if the Pt amount is close to 50 at.% and processing conditions favor the complete formation of the L10 phase; deviations in composition or processing that lead to phase inhomogeneities could undermine the effect.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain and may depend on subtle processing parameters. Variations in thermal treatment or phase stability could influence the outcome.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of equiatomic FeCoNiMnCu high-entropy alloy and a second set with approximately 50 at.% Pt added. Process both sets under identical sputtering and rapid thermal annealing conditions. Use X-ray diffraction to verify the presence of the L10 phase in the Pt-doped samples and confirm the high-symmetry phase in the baseline samples.
measurements: X-ray diffraction for phase identification and confirmation of L10 ordering
Vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) or SQUID magnetometry to measure coercive fields
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pt-doped samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in coercive field relative to the baseline, and/or if XRD fails to confirm the formation of a distinct L10 ordered phase, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: While the combination of saturation magnetization and coercivity for these RTA‐ treated FeCoNiMnCu films is impressive in comparison to previously reported bulk systems, the coercivity is still modest, due to the high symmetry of the cubic lattice which limits the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy. The facilitation of low‐symmetry chemical order and crystal structure combined with strong spin‐orbit coupling is in general necessary to realize strong magnetocrysalline anisotropy. To achieve these conditions in a high entropy system, we have added 50 at.% Pt to the FeCoNiMnCu alloy, employing the high entropy intermetallic design approach in search of highly anisotropic L10 ordering. Although the certainty of Pt sites reduces the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, we demonstrate below that such optimized entropy can still stabilize a single high‐entropy L10 phase.

In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

reading.lever: Introduce ~50 at.% Pt to induce an L10 ordered phase, lowering symmetry and enhancing spin–orbit coupling.
reading.why: This composition change directly addresses the intrinsic limitation of cubic symmetry that hampers coercivity and is supported by evidence in Pt-doped high‐entropy films.
